clue.text: Giving publicity to one boxing?

indicators.note: a boxer fights inside a ring, so this word asks for one letter placed within the words for that arena

parts.note: boxing takes place in a ring, so 'a ring' is the setting
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether boxing is a good way to make your name known.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'one boxing' as one in a ring: I goes inside A RING, giving AIRING. The question mark flags this loose wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Airing views or news means putting them before the public, broadcasting or voicing them openly.

clue.text: One habitually taking things did wrong in law

indicators.note: one set of letters is placed within another

parts.note: an act of parliament is a law

indicators.note: done wrong means set out incorrectly, so these letters need rearranging

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: 'Did wrong' looks like a phrase meaning 'offended', but 'did' is the fodder and 'wrong' scrambles it.
explanation.definitionFit: An addict regularly takes drugs or other substances, dependent on them by habit.

clue.text: A spinner of yarn can — true or false?

indicators.note: false means not genuine, so the letters are made up into something else

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Can a teller of tales be trusted, or is it all made up?
explanation.walkthrough: Spinning a yarn means telling a story, not working wool.
explanation.definitionFit: A raconteur is a skilled storyteller, someone who tells anecdotes entertainingly.

clue.text: A touching reminder

parts.note: surface reading: a moving memento that tugs the heartstrings
setter's reading: a prompt delivered by physical contact, such as with an elbow

explanation.walkthrough: 'Touching' seems to mean emotionally moving; it is literal physical contact.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudge is a gentle push with the elbow, given to prompt someone's memory or attention.

clue.text: No longer keen on pure cream

parts.note: to go off something is to stop liking it
white is the colour of purity

explanation.surface: Someone has lost their taste for unadulterated dairy cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen on' reads as one phrase, but 'on' only joins the wordplay to the definition, and 'cream' is a colour, not a dairy product.
explanation.definitionFit: Cream as a colour is a pale yellowish shade, exactly what off-white describes.

clue.text: American in charge of the match

parts.note: a charge or payment
abbreviation for United States, so American

explanation.surface: An American is put in charge of a sporting fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In charge' reads as a phrase meaning responsible, but the words split.
explanation.definitionFit: A fusee is a large-headed match that stays alight in wind, used by smokers outdoors.

clue.text: Guard what one says — a good maxim

parts.note: to watch over is to guard
a word is something said

explanation.surface: Be careful what you say: sound advice.
explanation.definitionFit: A watchword is a slogan or guiding principle that sums up a group's attitude.

clue.text: Nine getting half ration — he got revolutionary punishment

parts.note: Roman numeral for nine

indicators.note: half means only one of the two equal parts of the word is kept

parts.note: the final three of its six letters

explanation.surface: Someone receives a reduced allowance, a punishment of sorts.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Ixion was bound by Zeus to a fiery wheel that spun forever, hence 'revolutionary'.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeus punished this mythical king by binding him to an eternally turning wheel.

clue.text: Well held!

parts.note: surface reading: praise shouted for a good catch at cricket
setter's reading: held well, that is, regarded highly

explanation.walkthrough: 'Well held!' is the cricket cry for a fine catch; here it means held in high regard.
explanation.definitionFit: Esteemed describes someone respected and admired, held in high regard by others.

clue.text: Absconding child makes mischief

definitions.note: goings-on is plural, mischief a mass noun

parts.note: to abscond is to go off
a son is a child

explanation.definitionFit: Goings-on are dubious or improper activities, the sort of carry-on that counts as mischief.

clue.text: Such trees are barely recognisable in winter

definitions.text: Such trees are barely recognisable in winter

parts.words: Such trees are barely recognisable in winter
parts.note: surface reading: some trees are hard to identify in the cold season
setter's reading: the trees are bare, having shed their leaves for the winter

explanation.walkthrough: 'Barely' seems to mean 'hardly', but it hints that the trees stand bare.
explanation.definitionFit: Deciduous trees drop all their leaves each autumn, standing leafless until spring growth returns.

clue.text: Tobacco fraud

definitions.meaning: first meaning: tobacco sold as a ... roll of leaves

explanation.definitionFit: Twist is a form of pipe or chewing tobacco spun into a rope, and an old slang term for a cheat or swindle.

clue.text: Cutlery in military store

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a boxed set of knives, forks and spoons
second meaning: a shop or refreshment place on a military base

explanation.surface: Knives and forks are kept in an army storeroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A canteen of cutlery is a presentation case of tableware; a military canteen sells provisions to soldiers.

clue.text: There are two points he can possibly raise

parts.note: two compass points, east and north

indicators.note: possibly suggests one arrangement among many, so the letters may be reordered

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A man might be able to raise two matters for discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: Compass points are a standard source of single letters: here E and N.
explanation.definitionFit: To enhance something is to increase or improve its quality or value, lifting it higher.

clue.text: Nick's lawyer?

parts.note: surface reading: the solicitor of someone called Nick
setter's reading: Old Nick is a name for Satan, so this is Satan's legal representative

explanation.walkthrough: Old Nick is a traditional nickname for Satan.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names someone who argues the opposing side for argument's sake, literally Satan's counsel.

clue.text: Rebelling against authority, gets run in, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests one possible version among several, so the letters may be reordered

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Anyone defying authority ends up arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: To be run in is British slang for being arrested.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurgent is someone in revolt, rising up against an established government.

clue.text: Release a shipment

definitions.meaning: first meaning: rescue or setting free, as in deliverance
second meaning: a consignment of goods brought to someone

explanation.definitionFit: Delivery can mean liberation, as in 'delivery from evil', or a batch of goods handed over.

clue.text: Blend of main races

indicators.note: blending mixes ingredients together, so these letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A people formed by mixing the principal ethnic groups.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: the melting-pot nation.
explanation.definitionFit: The United States is often called a melting pot, its people descended from many ethnic origins.

clue.text: Well-known line in footwear

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the load line painted on a ship's hull

definitions.note: footwear is a mass noun, the answer one shoe
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a canvas gym shoe with a rubber sole

explanation.walkthrough: A plimsoll is a British term for a canvas gym shoe; the Plimsoll line marks how deep a laden ship may sit.
explanation.definitionFit: The Plimsoll line is the famous safety marking on ships, and the plimsoll a rubber-soled sports shoe.

clue.text: Wild flowers that aren't common

parts.note: surface reading: rare plants of the countryside
setter's reading: not commoners, that is, members of the nobility

explanation.walkthrough: The plant is in fact common in British hedgerows; 'common' here means belonging to the common people.
explanation.definitionFit: Lords-and-ladies is a British country name for wild arum, cuckoo-pint, a hedgerow plant with a hooded spathe.

clue.text: Be there at the start and finish

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter alone

parts.note: the opening letter of this word
a finish is an end

explanation.surface: Be present from the beginning to the very end.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend an event is to be present at it, to show up and be there.

clue.text: Senior accountant's holiday spot

parts.note: major means greater or elder, as in a senior partner
chartered accountant, abbreviated

explanation.surface: A high-ranking accountant chooses where to take a vacation.
explanation.walkthrough: CA, chartered accountant, is a professional qualification.
explanation.definitionFit: Majorca is a Spanish Mediterranean island hugely popular with package tourists from Britain.

clue.text: Pot roast?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a cannabis cigarette, slang for marijuana smoked
second meaning: a large cut of meat for roasting

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pot roast' is a dish of braised meat, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A joint is a rolled cannabis cigarette and also a cut of meat cooked whole.

clue.text: Played first part of hymn in a modern recording

parts.note: taken as written
compact disc
the hymn Te Deum opens with this word

explanation.surface: A performer played the opening of a hymn on a new recording.
explanation.walkthrough: The Te Deum is a Latin hymn of praise; its first word supplies the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Acted means played a part on stage or screen, performed as an actor does.

clue.text: Composer goes to court for judgment

indicators.note: one item heading towards the next means they sit side by side in sequence

parts.note: Giuseppe Verdi, Italian opera composer
standard abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A composer takes a legal case and awaits the ruling.
explanation.definitionFit: A verdict is the decision reached by a jury or judge at the end of a trial.

clue.text: Check key in, as a rule

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
a musical key

explanation.surface: Generally speaking, always check you've put your key in.
explanation.definitionFit: A reign is a monarch's period of rule, or sovereignty exercised over a realm.

clue.text: Oil producer under pressure has a heart of stone

definitions.text: Oil producer under pressure has a heart of stone

parts.words: Oil producer under pressure has a heart of stone
parts.note: surface reading: a harried oil executive is ruthless
setter's reading: a fruit that yields oil when pressed, with a stone at its centre

explanation.walkthrough: The oil producer sounds like a company, but it is a fruit that is pressed for its oil and has a stone at its core.
explanation.definitionFit: The olive is a stone fruit, a drupe, crushed in presses to extract its oil.

clue.text: Stop injured miner going into gallery

indicators.note: entering means one set of letters goes inside another

parts.note: the Tate, the London art gallery

indicators.note: something injured is damaged out of its proper shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Work must halt after a pit worker is hurt and taken to a gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a national art gallery in London; the rearranged letters sit inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To terminate is to bring to an end or halt, as with a contract or a service.

clue.text: Such tolerance may be a matter of degree

definitions.meaning: first meaning: freedom or leeway allowed

definitions.text: may be a matter of degree
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a geographic position north or south, measured in degrees

explanation.walkthrough: 'A matter of degree' is an idiom for something varying by amount, but here it is literal: geographic position measured in degrees.
explanation.definitionFit: Latitude means scope or freedom of action, and also angular distance from the equator.

clue.text: Mint that's still unwrapped?

parts.note: surface reading: a sweet that nobody has unwrapped yet
setter's reading: mint condition, as with a stamp or item never put to use

explanation.walkthrough: A mint sweet is wrapped, but 'mint' as in mint condition means never handled.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in mint condition is pristine and has not yet been handled or employed at all.
